info.title: loadbearing
info.description: One architecture spec, two render targets. LoadBearing checks a .NET solution against a fluent C# architecture spec — every rule carries a posture: Enforce for the law, Migrate for ratcheted debt with a grandfathered baseline, Quarantine for code contained rather than touched — and generates AI-agent context (a managed AGENTS.md block, MCP tools via 'loadbearing mcp') so the rules agents read are provably the rules the build enforces. Built for big, long-lived, business-critical .NET codebases.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Evaluate rules against a target solution; a project that fails to load, or whose NuGet packages did not resolve, fails the run (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the machine-readable JSON document instead of human-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --diff-base
options.description: A git ref; files changed since it are checked against quarantined scopes (Quarantine tripwire) — warnings only, never failures.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Check against the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of failing the run with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --sarif
options.description: Write a SARIF 2.1.0 report to <path> (GitHub code scanning et al.); human/--json output is unchanged.

options.name: --rules
options.description: Check only the rules whose ID matches these globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed and it spans '/'); the report, the summary counts and the 0/1 verdict then cover that subset alone. A filter matching no rule refuses the run (exit 2) and lists the available rule IDs.

options.name: --overview
options.description: Summarize the --json report at overview grain: every rule and every violation, with each violation's sites replaced by their count — coarser, not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --skeleton
options.description: Summarize the --json report at skeleton grain: the verdict alone — every rule with its prose, status, baseline and warnings, its violations replaced by their count. Coarser than --overview, and still not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --index
options.description: Summarize the --json report at index grain: a verdict per rule ID — posture, status, baseline, warnings and violation count — with the rule's prose and the workspace diagnostics elided (workspaceDiagnosticCount says how many) and every trust stamp kept. The coarsest grain, and the menu --rules globs pick from; still not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --binlog
options.description: A .binlog from a real build of this solution on this machine. Replays the captured structure instead of a design-time build; the capture persists, and later runs replay it automatically while structurally valid.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: render
commands.description: Render the managed AGENTS.md block(s) from the spec; a project that fails to load, or whose NuGet packages did not resolve, refuses the command (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Render from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing the command with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --diagram
options.description: Also render two Mermaid diagrams into <path>'s managed block: the codebase graph (projects and their cross-project references; solid = observed, dotted = declared but unobserved), then the spec's law (the places it names, what they must not reference, and the debt it grandfathers). The graph draws the projects the solution file declares, so a project a ProjectReference dragged into the build is not drawn; `graph` lists every loaded project and says which is which.

options.name: --diagram-only
options.description: Draw only the declared projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed) — for legibility on a large solution, not to keep a foreign project out. Scopes the codebase survey fence only, never the law fence. With --diagram.

options.name: --diagram-exclude
options.description: Drop the declared projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed) — for legibility on a large solution, not to keep a foreign project out. Scopes the codebase survey fence only, never the law fence. With --diagram.

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

commands.name: baseline
commands.description: Grandfather, shrink, or add one attributed exception to the ratcheted baselines; a project that fails to load, or whose NuGet packages did not resolve, refuses the command (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --init
options.description: Grandfather each ratcheted rule's current violations into its baseline (uncaptured rules only). [default: False]

options.name: --accept-reductions
options.description: Remove baseline entries whose violations no longer occur; never adds. [default: False]

options.name: --add
options.description: Grandfather exactly one currently observed violation of a captured rule, with attribution. [default: False]

options.name: --rule
options.description: The ratcheted rule ID to add the entry to (with --add).

options.name: --because
options.description: Why this entry is grandfathered — recorded in the baseline entry (single line; with --add).

options.name: --source
options.description: The referencing type of the edge to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID (with --add).

options.name: --target
options.description: The referenced type of the edge to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID, or a banned member's full name (System.DateTime.Now) or member symbol ID (P:System.DateTime.Now) (with --add).

options.name: --subject
options.description: The offending type of the shape violation to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID (with --add).

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Write baselines from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing the command with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

commands.name: graph
commands.description: Summarize the codebase: projects, declared vs observed project references, namespace inventory, and grouped external references. Needs no spec; a project that fails to load or to restore refuses the survey (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the machine-readable JSON survey document instead of human-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Survey the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --binlog
options.description: A .binlog from a real build of this solution on this machine. Replays the captured structure instead of a design-time build; the capture persists, and later runs replay it automatically while structurally valid.

options.name: --overview
options.description: Summarize at overview grain: the whole survey with each project's namespace inventory elided — coarser, not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --skeleton
options.description: Summarize at skeleton grain: the structural spine only — every project with its declared references and type count, and the observed project edges. Namespace inventories and external references are both elided, the latter reported as a count. Coarser than --overview, and still not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --index
options.description: Summarize at index grain: the project roster only — every project with its solution membership and type count, its declared references and target frameworks elided, and the observed edges and workspace diagnostics each reported as a count. The coarsest grain, and the menu --projects globs pick from; still not narrower. [default: False]

options.name: --projects
options.description: Survey only the projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed); references in both directions are kept, so an edge can name a project outside the scope. A filter matching no project refuses the survey (exit 2) and lists the available names.
